events.title: Eiffel Tower Officially Inaugurated
events.description: Gustave Eiffel climbed the tower's 1,710 steps to raise the French tricolour at the summit, marking the completion of the structure built for the 1889 Exposition Universelle in Paris. At 300 meters, it was the tallest man-made structure in the world.
events.significance: The tower became the enduring symbol of Paris and France and demonstrated the potential of wrought-iron engineering, remaining the world's tallest structure until 1930.

events.title: Birth of René Descartes
events.description: The French philosopher, mathematician, and scientist was born in La Haye en Touraine, France. He later authored Discourse on the Method and Meditations on First Philosophy, which contain the famous statement 'Cogito, ergo sum' (I think, therefore I am).
events.significance: Descartes is regarded as the father of modern Western philosophy and founded analytic geometry, linking algebra and geometry through the Cartesian coordinate system.

events.title: Hawke's Bay Earthquake Strikes New Zealand
events.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck the Hawke's Bay region of New Zealand's North Island, devastating the cities of Napier and Hastings. Around 256 people were killed and fires destroyed much of Napier's commercial center.
events.significance: It remains New Zealand's deadliest natural disaster in recorded history. The rebuilding of Napier in the Art Deco style created one of the world's most notable collections of 1930s architecture and led to stricter building codes in New Zealand.

events.title: Daylight Saving Time First Observed in the United States
events.description: The United States first observed daylight saving time on March 31, 1918, after Congress passed the Standard Time Act, which also established time zones. The measure was intended to conserve fuel and energy during World War I.
events.significance: The act established standardized time zones across the country and introduced the practice of seasonal clock changes, which continues to be debated and practiced in many nations today.

events.title: The 14th Dalai Lama Crosses into India
events.description: Following the failed Tibetan uprising against Chinese rule, Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, crossed the border into India after a perilous journey across the Himalayas and was granted asylum by the Indian government.
events.significance: This event began the Tibetan government-in-exile based in Dharamshala, India, and brought international attention to the Tibetan cause, which remains a major issue in global politics and human rights discussions.
